title: Indicating an interchange on the label under M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D and 247 CMR 9.05(3)
rule_summary: M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D, after directing that, except where the practitioner has indicated 'no substitution', the pharmacist dispense an interchangeable abuse deterrent product if one exists or, if none exists, a less expensive, reasonably available, interchangeable drug product, provides that the pharmacist shall also indicate on the label the fact of the interchange in the following manner: 'Interchange (name of exact drug product dispensed)'. Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(a), when a less expensive generic drug product has been dispensed, the words 'interchange' plus the generic name and manufacturer of the product shall appear on the label, in the manner '"Interchange": (Generic name of less expensive drug product dispensed plus manufacturer)'. Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(b), when a less expensive brand name drug product has been dispensed, the words 'interchange' plus either the generic name and manufacturer of the product or the less expensive brand name dispensed shall appear on the label. Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(c), in addition, the brand name of the prescribed drug product may also appear on the label, in a form that follows the product actually dispensed with the word 'for' and a brand name. Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(d), abbreviations are permissible as long as they are commonly understood; for example, 'IC' may be used for 'interchange' and manufacturers' names may be abbreviated as shown in the Massachusetts List of Interchangeable Drugs. Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(e), 247 CMR 9.05 shall only apply to prescriptions dispensed by a pharmacy with a Drug Store Pharmacy License.
exam_relevance: Tests that an interchange is shown on the label itself, what follows the word 'interchange' when a less expensive generic or brand name product is dispensed, that the prescribed brand name may also appear, and that commonly understood abbreviations such as 'IC' are permitted.

authority.name: Massachusetts General Laws, prescriptions of interchangeable drug products
Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy, interchangeable drugs labeling

exceptions: Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(e), 247 CMR 9.05, its labeling paragraph included, shall only apply to prescriptions dispensed by a pharmacy with a Drug Store Pharmacy License.
common_confusions: Leaving the interchange off the label because the patient was told of it. Section 12D requires the fact of the interchange to be indicated on the label.
Showing a less expensive generic product by its generic name alone. 247 CMR 9.05(3)(a) requires the generic name and manufacturer of the product.
Treating the prescribed brand name as required. Under 247 CMR 9.05(3)(c) it may also appear.
Treating every abbreviation as forbidden. 247 CMR 9.05(3)(d) permits abbreviations that are commonly understood, such as 'IC' for 'interchange'.
verification_notes: Read in the current text of M.G.L. c. 112, § 12D on malegislature.gov and in the current 247 CMR 9.00 published on mass.gov (page footers dated 12/6/24) on 2026-09-16.
